title: Unauthenticated DoS: integer user API public key triggers RSA key generation
summary:
Passing an integer to `OpenSSL::PKey::RSA.new` generates a new RSA keypair of that bit length rather than parsing an existing key. Several endpoints fed the unvalidated `public_key` request param straight into this call, so an unauthenticated attacker could send a large integer (e.g. a multi-kilobit "key") and force the server to spend seconds generating a keypair per request, tying up Puma workers and degrading or denying service.

The most severe path was `ApplicationController#redirect_to_login_if_required`, which handled `user_api_public_key` on anonymous requests with no rate limiting. The user API key client creation endpoint and the device auth flow had the same pattern.

### Workarounds

None. Sites can mitigate by rate-limiting unauthenticated requests at the proxy, but the vulnerable paths ran before rate limiting on the worst endpoint.

Discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, as vulnerability ANT-2026-DJF9HY4Q.
